title: One-command install with locked, hashed dependencies
notes: Found 2026-11-22 installing tadu on a shared VPS for casegpt (casegpt commit 7dab3f1). PyPI has only 0.1.0, without format 2, so the install had to be uv tool install git+https://github.com/syntopica/tadu@<commit>. That pins tadu but resolves its 19 dependencies (cryptography, requests, requests-oauthlib, werkzeug, limits and others) fresh at install time, which a security review flagged as a supply-chain risk on a shared account. Most of them serve only the board's sign-in.

2026-11-22: done in code, waiting on a release. The six sign-in libraries moved to the github extra (plain install: filelock and platformdirs only; board --auth github without them stops with a message). release/hashed_requirements.sh writes the hashed files from uv.lock and dist/, and publish.yml attaches tadu-requirements.txt and tadu-github-requirements.txt to the GitHub release; the README documents pip install --require-hashes. Verified locally on a built 0.2.0 wheel: hashed install brings 3 packages, a tampered hash is refused, the github file brings the sign-in libraries. uv tool install ignores hashes in -c and --with-requirements (tested), so the command uses pip. Close once Publish tadu 0.2.0 has run and the release assets install.
done_when: A documented single command installs a released tadu with every dependency pinned by hash (a published requirements file with hashes or a uv lock), and the plain CLI install does not pull the board's sign-in libraries
